en: Title: *Trikāyastava Author: Nāgārjuna Source: Unpublished transcript with notes by John Newman, posted on academia.edu

He who is neither one nor many, the foundation for the great perfection of the welfare of self and others, neither non-existence nor existence, like space, of equal taste, and whose nature is difficult to discern.

I pay homage to that incomparable Dharmakāya of the Victors, which is untainted, changeless, auspicious, peerless, all-pervading, free from conceptual proliferation, and to be realized within each individual self.
(1) It transcends the world, is inconceivable, and is the sovereign manifestation of the self, the fruit of hundreds of well-performed deeds.
In the midst of the assembly, he proclaims a great and manifold [teaching] for the sake of delighting the wise;

I here pay homage to that Saṃbhogakāya of the Buddhas, which has spread throughout all worlds as the unceasing and noble sound of the True Dharma, and is established in the great kingdom of Dharma. 2.
For the sake of maturing sentient beings, he appears in some places blazing like fire; yet in others, he is seen again as utterly tranquil.
Engaged in manifold forms through various means, he removes the fear of the three realms of existence.

I pay homage to those three bodies of the Sugatas—the Nirmāṇakāya which extends throughout the ten directions for the great benefit of the Munis; the [Sambhogakāya] whose sole activity is the welfare of sentient beings; and the [Dharmakāya] consisting of the methods of immeasurable great wisdom and merit, which are beyond the path of mind and speech.

Having made this prostration with devotion, whatever merit I have accumulated as the seed of enlightenment—by that, having attained the three bodies, may I establish this entire world upon the path to awakening. 4.
